records.label: 11 PEPD families and 2 sporadic cases
quotes: A genome-wide linkage search followed by mutational analysis of the candidate gene SCN9A, which encodes hNa(v)1.7, identified eight missense mutations in 11 families and 2 sporadic cases.
an inherited condition characterized by paroxysms of rectal, ocular, or submandibular pain with flushing

records.label: 77 individuals from 15 families
quotes: Seventy-seven individuals from 15 families were identified. The onset of the disorder is in the neonatal period or infancy and persists throughout life.
Autonomic manifestations predominate initially, with skin flushing in all and harlequin color change and tonic attacks in most. Dramatic syncopes with bradycardia and sometimes asystole are common.
Later, the disorder is characterized by attacks of excruciating deep burning pain often in the rectal, ocular, or jaw areas, but also diffuse.

records.label: 3-year-old girl (proband)
records.segregation: inherited from father, who also carries the mutation and has jaw pain while yawning
quotes: Here we describe a 3-year-old child with a rare clinical picture of PEPD. Extremely painful voiding had been present since the child's birth.
The diagnosis was confirmed by the detection of a heterozygous pathogenic mutation in the SCN9A gene, c.554G>A (p.Arg185His) inherited paternally.
Significant reduction of the pain was achieved with carbamazepine.
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

quotes: The same mutation was also found in the girl's father, who has occasionally had some pain in his jaw while yawning since childhood.

notes.statement: Meglič et al. (2014) reported that carbamazepine significantly reduced the pain in a 3-year-old girl with PEPD who had extremely painful voiding.
quotes: Significant reduction of the pain was achieved with carbamazepine.

notes.statement: Meglič et al. (2014) noted that the SCN9A R185H mutation found in their PEPD patient and her father had also been reported in patients with small fiber sensory neuropathy. They suggested that intra- and interfamilial phenotypic variability associated with gain-of-function Nav1.7 variants may explain this.
quotes: The case is interesting because the same mutation as that found in the girl and her father has been found in patients with small fiber sensory neuropathy.
intra- and interfamily phenotypic diversity in symptoms associated with a gain-of-function variant of Na(V)1.7 are also described and may explain our case

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) described paroxysmal extreme pain disorder, previously called familial rectal pain syndrome, as an autosomal dominant sodium channelopathy involving SCN9A.
quotes: an autosomal dominant condition recently shown to be a sodium channelopathy involving SCN9A

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) found that attacks of pain were triggered by factors such as defecation, cold wind, eating, and emotion, and that the disorder persisted throughout life.
quotes: Attacks are triggered by factors such as defecation, cold wind, eating, and emotion.

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) found that carbamazepine was effective in almost all patients who tried it, but the response was often incomplete.
quotes: Carbamazepine is effective in almost all who try it, but the response is often incomplete.

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) noted that the disorder is most likely to be misdiagnosed as epilepsy and, particularly in infancy, as hyperekplexia and reflex anoxic seizures.
quotes: It is most likely to be misdiagnosed as epilepsy and, particularly in infancy, as hyperekplexia and reflex anoxic seizures.

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2007) proposed the name paroxysmal extreme pain disorder for the condition previously called familial rectal pain syndrome.
quotes: To describe the clinical phenotype of paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (previously called familial rectal pain syndrome)

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) described paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEPD), previously known as familial rectal pain, as an inherited condition characterized by paroxysms of rectal, ocular, or submandibular pain with flushing.
quotes: Paroxysmal extreme pain disorder (PEPD), previously known as familial rectal pain (FRP, or OMIM 167400), is an inherited condition characterized by paroxysms of rectal, ocular, or submandibular pain with flushing.

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) performed a genome-wide linkage search in PEPD families, followed by mutation analysis of the candidate gene SCN9A.
quotes: A genome-wide linkage search followed by mutational analysis of the candidate gene SCN9A, which encodes hNa(v)1.7, identified eight missense mutations in 11 families and 2 sporadic cases.

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) found by in vitro functional analysis that 3 PEPD-associated mutant Nav1.7 channels showed reduced fast inactivation, leading to persistent sodium current, in contrast to primary erythermalgia mutations, which cause more negative activation thresholds. They concluded that PEPD and PE are allelic variants with distinct biophysical mechanisms.
quotes: Functional analysis in vitro of three of these mutant Na(v)1.7 channels revealed a reduction in fast inactivation, leading to persistent sodium current.
PEPD and PE are allelic variants with distinct underlying biophysical mechanisms and represent a separate class of peripheral neuronal sodium channelopathy.

notes.statement: Fertleman et al. (2006) noted that carbamazepine is effective in PEPD but not in primary erythermalgia; in vitro, it selectively blocked the persistent current of PEPD mutants but did not affect the negative activation threshold of a PE mutant.
quotes: Carbamazepine, a drug that is effective in PEPD, but not PE, showed selective block of persistent current associated with PEPD mutants, but did not affect the negative activation threshold of a PE mutant.

notes.statement: Fertleman and Ferrie (2006) proposed that the disorder previously called familial rectal pain syndrome be renamed paroxysmal extreme pain disorder.
quotes: What's in a name--familial rectal pain syndrome becomes paroxysmal extreme pain disorder.

notes.statement: HAYDEN and GROSSMAN (1959) described rectal, ocular, and submaxillary pain in a family as a familial autonomic disorder related to proctalgia fugax.
quotes: Rectal, ocular, and submaxillary pain; a familial autonomic disorder related to proctalgia fugaz: report of a family.

notes.statement: Mann and Cree (1972) reported a condition they called familial rectal pain.
quotes: Familial rectal pain.
